newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS - Asia Motors unveils Brazil plan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Asia Motors unveils Brazil plan.

text.p: Asia Motors Co Ltd, taking quick advantage of Brazil's controversial, new incentives for carmakers, Monday unveiled plan to invest $500 million in a new plant, cashing in on the burgeoning vehicle demand by suburbanities.

The new factory, Asia Motors' first outside South Korea, will be up and running by 1999 and will produce 60,000 units a year of the company's Towner and Topic minivans, all of them for the Brazilian market, officials said.
Both models would serve Brazil's growing market for small passenger vehicles operating in the ever-growing suburbs of the country's huge cities.

"South Korea is expanding to conquer the world and Brazil is an important base," said Washington Armenio Lopes, president of Asia Motors do Brasil, the company's Brazilian subsidiary. "As well as its size and access to the rest of South America, its transforming economy is a good market for our products."
The new plant will be located in Camacari, Bahia state, in Brazil's northeastern region.

Last week, President Fernando Henrique Cardoso signed a decree offering tax breaks and import tariff reductions to manufacturers based in the impoverished northeast, as well as in equally underdeveloped north and center-west regions.
Cardoso, at a ceremony to announce the investment, defended the decree, saying it would help the government in its aim of bringing investments to Brazil's poorer regions.

Critics have said the decree will earn the president the support of Bahia's powerful political bosses in his battle to win re-election. It also angered Argentina which fears it may lure auto investments away from its shores.
As well as benefitting from the terms of the decree, the new Asia Motors plant would also use raw materials from a major petrochemicals complex located in Camacari, officials said.
Lopes said the company decided to invest in Brazil in October 1995 but only finalized the deal once the decree had been published last week.
The Bahia plant may be expanded to produce other models currently produced by Kia, the South Korean holding which owns Asia Motors, and for exports, Lopes said.
The Asia Motors is the latest in a string of international automakers setting up shop in Brazil to take advantage of previosly existing incentives for local producers.
Earlier this month Audi and its parent company Volkswagen announced a $750 million investment just days after General Motors said it would invest $1.25 billion plan for three new plants.
Auto investment in Brazil is expected to reach about $19 billion between now and the year 2000.
